name: Segmental Odontomaxillary Dysplasia

criteria.description: Unilateral enlargement of the maxillary bone with segmental involvement
Ipsilateral dental abnormalities including missing or malformed teeth
Overlying facial skin hyperpigmentation or thickening on the affected side
Radiographic evidence of thickened cortical bone and trabecular pattern alteration in the affected maxilla
Lack of systemic skeletal or neurological abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral maxillary enlargement with ipsilateral dental anomalies and supportive radiographic bone changes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not currently definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects one side of the maxilla with segmental distribution
Missing or malformed teeth on the affected side
searchTerms: missing or small teeth on one side

pathognomonic.notes: Localized skin changes over the affected maxillary region

common.symptomName: Facial asymmetry due to maxillary enlargement
searchTerms: uneven face due to jaw growth

common.symptomName: Delayed eruption of teeth on affected side
common.notes: Delayed dental development ipsilateral to maxillary changes
searchTerms: late tooth eruption on one side
slow tooth growth on affected side

common.notes: Localized gingival overgrowth on affected side
searchTerms: mild gum swelling on one side

occasional.notes: Due to maxillary expansion affecting nasal cavity
Underdevelopment of maxillary sinus on affected side
searchTerms: underdeveloped maxillary sinus on one side
small sinus cavity in upper jaw

occasional.notes: Mild discomfort related to bone expansion
Soft tissue swelling over affected maxilla
searchTerms: slight swelling on one side of face
minor facial swelling on affected side

rare.notes: Due to Eustachian tube dysfunction from maxillary involvement
searchTerms: conductive hearing problem on same side

rare.notes: Rare sensory changes in distribution of trigeminal nerve
Due to malformed teeth and poor oral hygiene

imaging: Unilateral maxillary bone enlargement with thickened cortical bone
Altered trabecular pattern in affected maxilla
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; etiology unknown
other: Clinical examination reveals facial asymmetry and dental anomalies
Histopathology shows normal bone architecture with increased thickness

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrous dysplasia involves replacement of normal bone with fibrous tissue
Usually affects multiple bones or is polyostotic
Involves enlargement of all tissues on one side of the face, including soft tissue and bone
More generalized than segmental odontomaxillary dysplasia

redFlags: Severe facial asymmetry causing functional impairment
Development of neurological symptoms such as trigeminal nerve dysfunction
references: Neville BW, et al. Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology. 4th Edition. 2015.
Gorlin RJ, et al. Syndromes of the Head and Neck. 4th Edition. 2001.
